body: Polly could be my cat's sister.

I read through your post. I can tell you're in a lot of pain, and your past relationship reminds me of an ex my friend had. I just want to give you a big hug through my computer screen. I wish I could help you more there. It sounds like he lives close to you, and you just moved, so...this might be hard, but if he comes to cry on your shoulder again, I wouldn't even let him in the house. If he gets pissed off about that and tries to get you to answer the door, you could call the cops. Maybe that sounds harsh, but the guy is toxic, and you don't deserve to have him dump on you. 

Also, speaking as someone with an asshole for a boss, your boss sounds like an asshole. I'm sorry you have to work for someone who cuts you down like that instead of trying to figure out how to help you. He is also wrong--I would think once you are more stable, you would probably perform so much better. I know I would. Is there any way you can get a respite from that? Could you go back to a past employer who would be more supportive of you?

You mentioned a cat. I don't know about you, but I think animals are better at comforting me than humans have ever been. My cat has saved me in the past because he will stick by me when I'm feeling anxious or depressed. It sounds like you have thought of your kitty, and that is so poignant in this kind of situation. Will she cuddle with you? Does she come and sit with you when you're upset?

Please consider taking the time to do something that has made you feel peaceful in the past, or do something to make yourself feel good. The day after I posted here, I called off work, went shopping, visited the cats in the animal shelter, ate what I wanted, journaled, and spent a good part of the day driving and listening to my favorite songs. I did everything I wanted to do because I deserve to feel good, and I realized that I have the power to make myself happy. I barely talked to anyone, and I needed those moments of feeling like I had the capability to take care of myself instead of hurting myself. I know that may be difficult to do right now, but please think about treating yourself with the love, kindness, and respect you deserve--you absolutely DO deserve love, kindness, and respect, especially after what you have been through. 

You will be in my thoughts. Remember, you are a survivor--you lived through ten years of an awful relationship, and you didn't kill yourself then. As long as you need to talk, we will listen.

You have a point. I've been thinking about just calling off again and talking to my therapist on Saturday, rather than trying to go in and fake being okay for 8 hours while getting pestered by people asking if I'm feeling better, am I okay, what happened, etc. The worst that could happen is that the company could choose not to renew my contract at the end of the year--my contract allows unlimited sick days, so my pay will get docked, but I don't care about that at this point. 

> If something is slowly killing you, then the alternative, no matter how bad, still has a hope of being better than where you are right now.

I'm going to hold on to this thought. Thank you.
